headline: Real yields hold the long end high as CPI arrives

dek.text: Since Sep 1 the 10Y has moved {since-sep1-nominal-10y}, all of it real yield ({since-sep1-real-10y}); the breakeven moved {since-sep1-be-10y} even with Brent settling at ${brent-settle}.

thesis.text: Rates are the week's organizing force, and so far they are a real-rate story. The 10Y par yield ended Friday at {treasury-10y}, a few basis points under Monday's {treasury-10y-w41-high}, and the 30Y at {treasury-30y}. New supply has repriced with it: last week's 10-year auction cleared at {auction-10y} and the 30-year at {auction-30y}, against {auction-10y-sep} and {auction-30y-sep} in September.
thesis.uncertainty: A par-curve breakeven also carries inflation-risk and liquidity premia, so a flat breakeven is not proof that inflation expectations are anchored.
thesis.alternative: A rising term premium, not expected policy, may be what lifts real yields; daily par curves cannot separate the two.

thesis.text: Equities absorbed it by rotating, not falling. SPY returned {spy-week} on the week; semiconductors returned {smh-week}, regional banks {kre-week} and homebuilders {xhb-week}; utilities ({xlu-week}), staples ({xlp-week}) and energy ({xle-week}) led. Credit did not flinch (high yield {hyg-week}), and the VIX closed at {vix}, above SPY's 20-session realized volatility of {spy-realized-20}.

The tension: the Fed's minutes pointed to another hike, consumers' year-ahead inflation expectations rose to {umich-1y}, and the CPI consensus has energy lifting the headline while core stays subdued. Soft core with flat breakevens gives the long end room to ease and the rate-sensitive laggards room to run. Inflation compensation joining real yields would give the long end a second engine.

take.text: This is a real-rate regime with calm inflation pricing; a CPI week in which breakevens rise more than real yields fall would show it wrong.

spotlights.title: Real rates, not inflation pricing, set the long end

paragraphs.text: Since Sep 1 the 10Y real yield has moved {since-sep1-real-10y} while the 10Y breakeven stayed between {be-10y-range-low} and {be-10y-range-high}. Last week fit the pattern: the real 10Y moved {real-10y-change} and the breakeven {be-10y-change}. Oil did not change it either; WTI went from {wti-settle-prior-week} to {wti-settle} over the week and Brent settled at {brent-settle}.

It is not only a U.S. story. The UK 10Y gilt yields {intl-uk-10y}, above the U.S. {treasury-10y}, and France's 10Y ({intl-fr-10y}) yields more than Italy's ({intl-it-10y}), with press coverage of French debt stress. Germany ({intl-de-10y}) and Japan ({intl-jp-10y}) sit far lower.
paragraphs.uncertainty: Foreign yields are one-time readings from a secondary site, dated Friday; they are context, not admitted evidence.

paragraphs.text: This week CPI and PPI are the first inflation prints since the long end reached these levels, and there is no coupon supply to blur the reaction.

spotlights.why: Selected because it is the largest measured move behind the week's biggest scheduled catalyst. Considered and not featured: Japan and the yen (USD/JPY {usdjpy} at Friday's last quote; no post-reopen prints, and Japanese markets are closed Monday) and the dollar (DXY {dxy}).

spotlights.title: The weak spots meet their catalysts

paragraphs.text: Last week's two worst groups face direct tests. Semiconductors returned {smh-week} while the Nasdaq-100 returned {qqq-week}; ASML reports Wednesday and TSMC Thursday. Regional banks returned {kre-week} as the money-center banks report Tuesday and Wednesday.

Concentration is fading at the margin rather than breaking: QQQ's twenty-session spread over SPY is still {qqq-20s-vs-spy}, and equal weight's is {rsp-20s-vs-spy}. About half of tech's lost lead last week came from early-September sessions leaving the window, not from new selling.
The tell is tech-specific volatility: QQQ's 30-day implied volatility reached {lab-qqq-iv-oct8} at Thursday's close and eased to {lab-qqq-iv} on Friday, while SPY's sits at {lab-spy-iv}.

spotlights.why: Selected because SMH and KRE were last week's largest relative moves and each meets its own catalyst this week.

lab.test: On CPI day, do XLRE, XLU and IWM move against the 10Y? They still trail SPY over twenty sessions (XLRE {xlre-20s-vs-spy}, IWM {iwm-20s-vs-spy}), but the day-to-day link with the 10Y has been weak.
lab.weaken: Two of the three beat SPY over twenty sessions while the 30Y stays in the mid-5s.

lab.test: ASML and TSMC. QQQ's twenty-session spread over SPY is {qqq-20s-vs-spy}; semis start the week after a {smh-week} week.
lab.weaken: QQQ − SPY reaches zero, or equal weight stops trailing, at Friday's close.

lab.test: Does the VIX stay below 17 through CPI? It closed at {vix}. A lab observation, not yet a finding: QQQ's implied volatility rose to {lab-qqq-iv-oct8} on Oct 8 while SPY's barely moved.
lab.weaken: Two VIX closes at or above 17 in the week.

scenarios.name: Soft core, steady breakevens
scenarios.looks: Core CPI at or below consensus; real yields ease; rate-sensitives and equal weight lead; semis stabilize after TSMC.
scenarios.first: Wednesday's XLRE, IWM and RSP prints against SPY in this brief; Thursday's curve page shows a lower real 10Y with the breakeven near {be-10y}.

scenarios.name: Inflation joins real rates
scenarios.looks: Core above consensus and breakevens rise with oil; the 2Y leads higher; the 10Y and 30Y push through {treasury-10y-w41-high} and {treasury-30y-w41-high}.
scenarios.first: IWM, KRE and XHB underperform on Wednesday; the VIX closes at or above 17; Thursday's curve shows breakevens up.
scenarios.breaks: Breakevens fall back while yields keep rising: that is the real-rate regime again, not this one.

scenarios.name: In line; earnings set the spreads
scenarios.looks: CPI near consensus; the 10Y stays inside last week's {treasury-10y-w41-low} to {treasury-10y-w41-high} range; the index drifts while bank and chip results move sectors.
scenarios.first: Index changes small next to XLF, KRE and SMH moves; VIX near {vix}.
scenarios.breaks: The 10Y leaves the range on a close.

scenarios.name: Hot headline, soft core
scenarios.looks: Energy lifts the headline while core stays soft; breakevens rise as real yields fall, leaving the 10Y little changed.
scenarios.first: Thursday's curve page: real 10Y down, breakeven up. Energy and gold lead; rate-sensitives split.
scenarios.breaks: Breakevens and real yields move the same way.
